detailed_description: The Keyboard Tester is a browser-based key event viewer for quick keyboard checks and JavaScript shortcut debugging. When this page has focus, it listens for keydown and keyup events, highlights matching keys on the visual keyboard, shows the latest key, code, and keyCode values, and keeps a short recent-key history that can be cleared. This is useful when checking whether a key reaches the browser, comparing physical key codes with displayed characters, or validating a simple shortcut layout before adding it to an app. It does not expose hardware scan codes, certify keyboard rollover, inspect operating-system drivers, or export a raw event log; it only shows the KeyboardEvent values that the browser provides to the page.
usage_steps: Click inside the page or keep the tool tab focused so browser keyboard events reach the tester.
Press a key and review the latest key, code, and keyCode values shown above the keyboard layout.
Hold a key or simple modifier combination to see the highlighted keys update on keydown and keyup.
Review the recent key history when comparing repeated presses or checking whether a shortcut sequence reached the page.
Use Clear to reset the short history before starting another keyboard or browser check.
usage_examples: A frontend developer checks whether a custom shortcut should listen for the displayed code value or the displayed key value.
A support agent asks a user to press Backspace, Enter, and arrow keys to confirm the browser is receiving those key events.
A game prototype author checks a simple WASD layout before wiring the same codes into movement controls.

faqs.question: What does the tester show for each key?
faqs.answer: It shows the browser-reported key, code, and legacy keyCode for the most recent key event, plus a short history of recent keys.

faqs.question: Can it certify keyboard ghosting or rollover?
faqs.answer: No. It can show which key events reach the browser during a quick check, but it is not a hardware certification or driver diagnostic tool.

faqs.question: Why do some shortcuts not appear?
faqs.answer: Browsers and operating systems reserve some combinations, so they may never reach the page. Test the exact browser and device you plan to support.

faqs.question: Should I type passwords into this page?
faqs.answer: No. Use harmless test keys only. The page is meant for event debugging, not for handling sensitive input.
